title: Hosted API queue surge investigation and proactive slot rebalancer
creator: Anita Patel
description: Follow-up investigation and remediation work after a hosted API capacity incident where tenant-driven bursts caused persistent GPU queue buildup and prolonged throttling. Goal: identify root causes for amplified queues, prototype a proactive slot rebalancer (soft-reclaim + fractional slot assignment), and land short-term mitigations to prevent recurrence during peak churn windows.
impact_summary: On 2025-11-12 a multi-tenant traffic spike produced sustained queue growth in two GPU pools resulting in elevated latency for 13% of requests and degraded throughput for several medium-priority customers. Estimated lost goodput: ~18% across affected pools during the 45-minute incident window. No data exfiltration; primary impact was availability and customer experience.
timeline: 2025-11-12T10:07Z - Alert: pool-nyc-3 queue depth exceeded soft watermark (90th percentile) for 10 minutes
2025-11-12T10:12Z - Autoscaler failed to trigger expected double-step due to hysteresis config; queue continued to grow
2025-11-12T10:23Z - Manual throttles applied to best-effort lanes; high-priority lanes still experienced tail latency spikes
2025-11-12T10:52Z - Pool recovered after instance redistribution and tenant-level admission caps were enforced
2025-11-13 - Initial incident review: identified two amplifying factors: tenant burstiness fingerprinting missing, and slot allocation logic too coarse for mixed small/large sessions
decision_log: Prioritize safety: short-term admission caps and jittered backoff rollout to all Hosted pools (target within 72 hours)

Prototype approach: build 'slot rebalancer' service that continuously adjusts fractional slot assignments per tenant based on recent inter-arrival and KV cache hit patterns rather than fixed slot counts
Reject full pool overprovisioning as a long-term cost strategy; focus on smarter packing + early-shedding for low-SLO tenants
Keep existing autoscaler hysteresis but add a 'probe' policy triggered by burst fingerprints to allow faster single-step scale-up for substantiated surges
action_items: ANALYSIS-1 (Marco): Add burst fingerprint metric to request pipeline (inter-arrival distribution + token-rate delta) and surface in existing pool dashboards - 2d
REBALANCER-1 (Nina): Prototype slot rebalancer that supports fractional slots and soft-reclaim (safely drop from 1.0 -> 0.6 fractional weight) - 4d
RUNBOOK-1 (SRE): Update runbook with steps to apply tenant-level soft caps and emergency re-route to dedicated pools - 1d
THROTTLE-1 (Infra): Ship jittered admission backoff middleware for best-effort lanes with deploy flag - 3d
TESTS-1 (QA): Create chaos test that synthetic-bursts a tenant and validates that slot rebalancer + autoscaler prevent queue amplification - 3d

2025-11-19 - Marco: Captured initial heap of telemetry and dashboards, found that heavy KV cache miss rates correlated with long sessions from two tenants.
2025-11-20 - Nina: Prototype design draft uploaded; using moving-window token-rate and cache-hit signals to compute fractional slot weights. Shared for initial feedback.
2025-11-21 - PM review (Evan): Asked to ensure tenant throttles are surfaced to billing/usage dashboards and communicated to affected customers via status page workflows.
2025-11-24 - SRE (Priya): Runbook patch reviewed; added emergency 'spill-to-dedicated' checklist and an owner rotation for incident windows.

postmortem_conclusion: Root cause was a combination of bursty tenant load patterns that our admission heuristics did not fingerprint, and slot allocation granularity that allowed long-lived sessions to monopolize a pool's effective concurrency. Remediation includes adding burst detection, deploying a slot rebalancer to spread fractional slot capacity, and short-term admission backoff. These combined changes should reduce amplification risk without large capacity increases.
notes_for_release: runtime-1.24 will include opt-in slot rebalancer, jittered admission middleware, and new dashboard panels for burst fingerprints. Scheduled canary in us-east-1 after QA sign-off.
